page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, providing dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a single 68 GB NVMe SSD, while no GPU accelerators are present. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and SHA-NI cryptography extensions, though it lacks Intel-specific AMX features.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, placing in the top tier for stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded text processing. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also register top-tier throughput. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with read-only large-block speeds at 48.96 GB/sec and write speeds at 33.42 GB/sec. For language model workloads, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 347.94 tokens/sec on small 135M models, but drops to a weak rating for prompt processing on medium 7B models.

The qualitative cost profile of the c4d-standard-8-lssd reflects a balanced resource density, combining dedicated AMD EPYC compute cores with high-speed local NVMe storage. This configuration avoids the overhead of network-attached storage for temporary files, making it a resource-efficient choice for workloads requiring fast local read/write operations. The server is well-suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and lightweight single-threaded processing tasks. However, the limited 31 GB memory capacity and average multi-core scaling make it less optimal for large-scale memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded parallel computing.
